### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A20, A28, A29 and A30 each ran in all 200 cases, at a mean event position of about 0.37; in the later window they are nearly absent — A20 appears in about 3 of 200 cases, A28 in 2, A29 in 1 and A30 in none. [OCC005, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, POS005, POS009, POS010, POS011]
- The old block's wiring disappears with it: A30 shows no observed outgoing transitions in the later window, the few remaining transitions of A20, A28 and A29 (1–3 observations each) lead elsewhere, and their co-occurrence with A15 and with each other falls from 100% of cases to about zero. [DIR008, DIR012, DIR013, DIR014, REL016, REL019, REL043]
- A different set of activities emerges in the later window: A19, A21, A22 and A23 rise from 0–1 of 200 cases to roughly 39–58 of 200 (about 20–29%), occupy a similar region of the case (mean positions about 0.37–0.39), and send about 90–100% of their observed outgoing transitions to A31. [OCC004, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, DIR007, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011]
- A46 reroutes: before, about 82 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A20, A28, A29 or A30; after, about 96 in 100 go to A19, A21, A22 or A23, and the distance from A46 to A31 shrinks from consistently 5 steps to about 2 steps in 93% of later pairs. [DIR015, LAG009, REL037, REL060]
- A04 becomes a frequent, early step: participation rises from 18% to 68% of cases (36 to 136), its median event position falls from about 0.32 to 0.25, and about 90 in 100 of its outgoing transitions now go to A16 (about 5 before), with A04 followed by A16 within one step in about 98% of observed pairs (14% before). [OCC002, POS001, DIR002, LAG001, REL002]
- A15 feeds this new A04 step: about 37 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions now go to A04 (under 1% before), while A15 to A16 falls from about 92% to 62%; A04 also now precedes A31, A46, A51 and A52 in about 62% of cases, where previously it mostly occurred without them. [DIR006, LAG004, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- A02 and A10 run less often: participation falls from about 21% to about 6% of cases for A02 (41 to 11) and from 21% to 8% for A10 (41 to 16); their rerouting profiles rest on only about 13–18 later observations. [OCC001, OCC003, DIR001, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the segment A20–A28–A29–A30 that previously ran in every case between A46 and A31 is no longer executed, that about a quarter of cases instead run one or more of A19, A21, A22 and A23 into A31, and that A04 has become a frequent step between A15 and A16. The participation changes are large and well supported (A30 in 200 of 200 earlier cases and none later; A19 in none earlier and 53 of 200 later; A04 in 36 versus 136 cases), the routing changes are direct (about 96 in 100 of A46's outgoing transitions now lead to the new activities, and about 90 in 100 of A04's lead to A16), and the relational evidence shows the new order directly (A04 precedes A31 and A46 in about 62% of later cases; A46 reaches A31 in about 2 steps instead of 5). Occurrence, routing, position and relation indicators agree, and even counting items about the same activities as one difference, the distinct differences clearly exceed the roughly 1.14 items expected by chance when screening 230 units. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC011, OCC002, DIR015, DIR002, REL011, LAG009, LAG001]

Competing explanations remain: the evidence cannot distinguish a rewiring of a single flow from a shift in the mix of pre-existing trace variants — the later window may simply contain more cases of a variant without the old block, which would look identical at this level — and zero participation only shows that an activity was not observed in that window. The rerouting details for the low-frequency activities A02, A08 and A10 rest on about 13–19 outgoing transitions in the later window, and the many occurrence, relation and position entries for A20, A28, A29 and A30 describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC003, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, REL016, REL019]
